elements.element: Customer owns Deliverables and work product created for Customer.
elements.evidence: The inserted paragraph gives Customer only a licence ("Kubient grants Customer a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free license to use, modify and sublicense... all deliverables"); no ownership vests in Customer, and retained warranty (viii) still states Kubient is "the rightful owner or licensee of all intellectual property rights to the Service, the Auction Platform and products delivered hereunder".

elements.element: Vendor assigns the Deliverables and work product to Customer.
elements.evidence: No assignment language appears anywhere in the rendered text; the insertion is a licence grant only.

elements.element: Vendor retains its pre-existing intellectual property.
elements.evidence: "Kubient retains ownership of its generic tools, know-how and the Auction Platform", and warranty (viii) confirms Kubient's ownership of the Service and Auction Platform; nothing divests Vendor's own IP.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Vendor IP embedded in Deliverables is perpetual.
elements.evidence: "a perpetual... license to use, modify and sublicense... all deliverables provided by Kubient hereunder other than the Auction Platform" — a deliverables licence necessarily reaches Vendor IP embedded in those deliverables (Auction Platform itself carved out and licensed separately under paragraph 2).

elements.element: Customer's licence to embedded Vendor IP is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: The grant is expressly "perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free".

elements.element: Customer's licence to embedded Vendor IP is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: "royalty-free license to use, modify and sublicense" in the inserted paragraph.

elements.element: Customer retains all rights in Customer Data.
elements.evidence: The insertion only limits Kubient's licence scope; there is no affirmative statement that Customer retains all right, title and interest in its Content, Requests and other data. Retained paragraph 25(a) allocates responsibility/liability for Content but not ownership of data.

elements.element: Any Vendor licence in Customer Data is limited to processing it solely to provide the Services.
elements.evidence: "Any license granted to Kubient in the Content, Requests, and any other data or materials belonging to, supplied by or processed for Customer is limited to processing the same solely to provide the Services" — catch-all covers every category of Customer data.

elements.element: The parties do not jointly own intellectual property.
elements.evidence: No no-joint-ownership statement was added; the insertion is silent on joint ownership.

elements.element: Vendor may retain ownership of generic tools and know-how.
elements.evidence: "Kubient retains ownership of its generic tools, know-how and the Auction Platform."

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is perpetual.
elements.evidence: "Kubient grants Customer a perpetual... license" to deliverables.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: "perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free license"; the revocability in paragraph 2 attaches only to the separately carved-out Auction Platform licence, so there is no internal inconsistency.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is worldwide.
elements.evidence: "worldwide" appears expressly in the grant.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: "royalty-free" appears expressly in the grant.

elements.element: Customer may use and modify Deliverables for its business.
elements.evidence: "license to use, modify and sublicense, for Customer's business, all deliverables provided by Kubient hereunder other than the Auction Platform"; paragraph 25(a)'s no-modification restriction is directed at "the Service"/"software included in any Service", which warranty (i) treats as distinct from "deliverables provided hereunder".

elements.element: Customer may sublicense Deliverables for its business.
elements.evidence: "and sublicense, for Customer's business" in the inserted grant; paragraph 2's "without right of sublicense" applies only to the Auction Platform, which the new grant expressly excludes.

elements.element: Any Vendor licence in Customer Data is limited to processing it solely to provide the Services.
elements.evidence: "Any license granted to Kubient in the Content, Requests, and any other data or materials belonging to, supplied by or processed for Customer is limited to processing the same solely to provide the Services" — no distribution, resale or wider "purposes contemplated" carve-out remains.

reasons: The finding of 'missing' is sound: the Agreement has no IP/data-ownership article, and the only grant to Customer (paragraph 2) is limited, non-sublicensable and revocable, which fails the fallback on material terms.

Fallback is position-complete: the single inserted paragraph delivers Vendor retention of generic tools/know-how, and a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables for Customer's business, plus a solely-to-provide-the-Services limit on any Kubient licence in Customer data.

Preferred is not complete: there is no Customer ownership of or assignment of Deliverables, no affirmative 'Customer retains all rights in Customer Data' sentence, and no express bar on joint ownership. To reach preferred the drafter would need to add (i) 'Kubient hereby assigns to Customer all right, title and interest in the deliverables and work product created for Customer', (ii) 'Customer retains all right, title and interest in Customer Data', and (iii) 'No intellectual property will be jointly owned.'

Minimal: the insertion is a concise new paragraph for a missing clause, deletes nothing, adds no survival tail, expense or procedural boilerplate, and the 'other than the Auction Platform' carve-out is necessary to avoid contradicting the retained paragraph 2 licence rather than an extra. The words 'and the Auction Platform' in the retention sentence lightly overlap with warranty (viii) but serve as the anchor for that carve-out.

Preserves intent: paragraph 2's Auction Platform licence, paragraph 25(a)'s use restrictions on the Service, and the Kubient warranties survive without contradiction, and no new assignment exception or Vendor-favourable transfer right is created.

Drafting caution to verify before sending: confirm 'Requests' is a defined term in the Agreement; if it is not, drop the capitalisation or delete it, since the catch-all 'any other data or materials belonging to, supplied by or processed for Customer' already carries the element and an undefined capitalised term risks a dangling reference.

system.text:
You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use document tools to inspect every responsive clause, definition, and cross-reference; do not stop at the first hit.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and never flag an obligation that benefits our party.

Keep rule boundaries precise. A sourcing requirement that applies only when Customer voluntarily uses Vendor's interface is not exclusivity when Customer is expressly free to use alternatives. A disclosure, right-to-match, or most-favoured offer mechanic belongs under MFN and is not also exclusivity unless it outright prohibits using alternatives after the mechanic is honoured. Natural-term non-renewal belongs under RENEWAL and is not Vendor mid-term termination for convenience under T4C; do not flag the same term twice. An unconditional Customer election to terminate is a convenience right even if the clause does not use the word "convenience". An auto-renewal clause that either party may terminate on notice does not establish that Vendor termination is term-end-only unless the effective date is expressly tied to the end of the then-current term. Under IP, inspect every Customer Data licence: distribution, resale, independent exploitation, or use for the broader "purposes contemplated by this Agreement" is not cured by adding a separate ownership sentence and must be narrowed expressly to processing solely to provide the Services. Processing to provide, secure, support, or improve the Services for Customer is service delivery, not independent exploitation. A prohibition on another use unless Customer later gives express written consent is not a standing Vendor licence; do not flag that hypothetical consent alone.

Do not weaken Customer while completing an element. A Customer licence-transfer right does not justify expanding a mutual assignment exception for Vendor; draft a Customer-only licence transfer. A conditional insurance element covering Customer Data must reach every category of data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for Customer; do not narrow it to a few named examples. When inserting qualifiers into an existing clause, keep every untouched word verbatim rather than cosmetically rewriting the whole sentence.

Resolve assignment and licence scope literally. For ASSIGN fallback, "other assignments require consent" means every non-successor assignment: a retained no-consent affiliate exception conflicts with that level, even when mutual. For LICENSE, first resolve whether the defined Customer already includes affiliates; do not add duplicate coverage. A licence grant to an entity ordinarily reaches that entity's authorized personnel, so do not rewrite a separate personnel/access clause unless it expressly prohibits use needed by the new grant. Express a permitted licence transfer directly (for example, "without Vendor's approval"); do not add a broad notwithstanding override of the assignment clause.

The preferred and fallback positions are operative checklists, not drafting themes. First classify under the supplied playbook semantics. If the existing bargain meets every fallback element on its material terms, submit compliant and do not upgrade it merely to reach preferred wording. If it genuinely fails fallback, choose a preferred or fallback target and make the shortest operative change that meets every element at that target level.

For every deviation or missing proposal, map each target element exactly once in elementCoverage. Before drafting, search for each element independently. Use already_met only with a verbatim document quote, cite that quote's paragraph in paragraphIds, and do not restate an already-met element in a new operation. Use addressed_by_operation with one-based operationIndexes. You may leave an element unaddressed only by submitting needs_review with a concrete explanation. Never claim that a margin comment cures missing operative language.

Draft surgically: replace only the existing words or sentence that need to change, group related elements into one operation, and preserve unrelated text. When curing a prohibition, edit the prohibitory operator and duration or use one short affirmative permission; do not both negate the restriction and recite every permitted activity. Avoid a broad "notwithstanding" override when a precise conforming edit can resolve the conflict. After rendering, inspect every retained reference to a term or sentence you changed: an undefined term, dangling cross-reference, or contradictory retained mechanic is an intent failure. Prefer a fallback edit when deleting to preferred would require collateral rewrites. A replace may add at most 1.5 times as many words as it removes. For a genuinely absent clause, use insert_after and draft the shortest clause that carries only the still-missing target elements; do not rewrite a neighbouring clause.

The atomic checklist is the ceiling as well as the floor. Model language and precedents are source material, not permission to add non-element boilerplate. Omit survival tails, at-own-expense language, incidental or special damages, procedures, and other ancillary terms unless a selected element requires them. Meet numeric floors and ceilings at the selected threshold; do not volunteer a more onerous duration or amount just because it appears at the other level. Preserve exact nouns, temporal anchors, and bases: "fees paid or payable" may not become broader "all amounts paid or payable", and "preceding the claim" is not interchangeable with "preceding the event giving rise to the claim." Preserve every word in a mixed phrase that the target does not require changing: for example, curing "without reduction or termination rights" must not silently remove the reduction restriction. A customary other-court carve-out solely for temporary injunctive relief does not defeat an otherwise exclusive merits forum. A preferred "no non-compete or field-of-use restriction" is not met while Vendor retains an exclusive right that prevents Customer from using or licensing its own product or brand. Do not add terms that are absent from the selected checklist.

For a preferred no-liquidated-damages result, make the prohibition unconditional and conform every retained formula, instalment, or "if any" payment mechanic; otherwise use the exact fallback cap instead. Defining a payment as zero while retaining machinery that contemplates it is not a clean cure.

For T4C, do not add "in whole or in part" or a partial-termination right unless the selected element and this contract's Order Form structure require it.

For TRANSITION, the selected assistance duration must be available after every covered expiry or termination; a pre-expiry request condition does not establish a post-termination duration. State that certified deletion occurs after data return, not merely after assistance. For WARRANTY fallback, a report or output conforming to a user manual is not a software-to-documentation warranty unless that report is itself the defined software deliverable; add the shortest express software conformance warranty when needed.

For a preferred liability cap, verify the definition behind every payment-carve-out noun. A carve-out limited to a narrowly defined "Fees" category does not exclude all Customer payment obligations; surgically use "amounts due" or equally comprehensive operative language. Do not add explanatory examples such as "including subscription fees" to the cap formula when lowercase fees under the Agreement and all Order Forms is sufficient.

Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Finding quotes must be 600 characters or fewer. Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and accurately explain the operative change.

For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding. For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

messages.content:
Parties: we represent The Associated Press; counterparty is Kubient Inc..

Rule and atomic checklists:
ID: AUDIT
Title: Audit rights against Customer
Kind: parametric
Summary: Audits of our usage must be rare, notified, off-site where possible and at the Vendor's cost.
Severity: medium
Category: audit
Position — preferred:
No more than once per 12 months, on 30 days' written notice, during business hours, by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, at Vendor's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5 %; no direct access to Customer systems.

Position — fallback:
Once per year on 15 days' notice; Vendor bears cost unless underpayment exceeds 10 %.
Position — walk-away:
Unlimited or unannounced audits, or remote access to Customer systems.
Detection guidance:
Find audit/inspection/verification rights binding Customer; extract frequency, notice, cost allocation, system access.
Redline guidance:
Insert the frequency/notice/cost limits with minimal edits; delete system-access language.

Preferred atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Vendor may audit no more than once in any 12-month period.",
  "Vendor must give at least 30 days' written notice of an audit.",
  "Audits occur during business hours.",
  "Audits are conducted by an independent auditor.",
  "The auditor is bound by confidentiality obligations.",
  "Audits are conducted off-site where possible.",
  "Vendor bears audit costs unless underpayment exceeds 5 percent.",
  "Vendor has no direct access to Customer systems for an audit."
]

Fallback atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Vendor may audit no more than once per year.",
  "Vendor must give at least 15 days' notice of an audit.",
  "Vendor bears audit costs unless underpayment exceeds 10 percent."
]

content.text:
**Finding submitted: deviation (T4C), fallback-level cure.**

- **Only responsive clause:** paragraph 4(a) (p0016). No other convenience-termination or early-termination-fee mechanic exists (4(b) is breach/insolvency; §5 is a revenue share with no prepaid fees; 4(c) is effects of termination).
- **What passes fallback:** AP has a 90-day for-any-reason exit after the Initial Term (which is exactly 12 months, so the lock-in is not itself a deviation), and the only termination-linked payment is fees generated during the 90-day termination period — within the three-months-of-fees cap.
- **What fails:** the right is mutual and not tied to term-end, so Kubient could exit for convenience mid-renewal-term. Rule and exact checklists:
ID: T4C
Title: Termination for convenience
Kind: parametric
Summary: We can leave on notice without penalty; the Vendor cannot walk away mid-term.
Severity: high
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Customer may terminate for convenience on 30 days' written notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees; Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.

Position — fallback:
Customer termination on 60–90 days' notice; early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees; Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term on 90 days' notice.

Position — walk-away:
No Customer right to terminate for convenience in a multi-year term; Vendor termination for convenience on fewer than 90 days' notice.

Detection guidance:
Find termination provisions. Determine which party may terminate without cause, the notice period, and any early-termination fee. Absence of any Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months is a deviation (kind: missing behaviour); a Vendor convenience right on short notice is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Add or edit a Customer convenience right (30 days), delete/limit Vendor's convenience right, replace penalties with the fallback fee cap.

Model language:
Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination.


Preferred atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.",
  "Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.",
  "Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.",
  "Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term."
]

Fallback atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.",
  "Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.",
  "Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.",
  "Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination."
]

Claimed finding status: deviation

Claimed target and element mapping:
{"level":"fallback","mappings":[{"element":"Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.","status":"addressed_by_operation","operationIndexes":[1]},{"element":"Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.","status":"already_met","quote":"Kubient shall be entitled to all fees generated during the termination period regardless of which Party terminates the Agreement"},{"element":"Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.","status":"addressed_by_operation","operationIndexes":[1]},{"element":"Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination.","status":"addressed_by_operation","operationIndexes":[1]}]}

Finding rationale:
Paragraph 4(a) is the only termination-for-convenience mechanic in the Agreement. It gives AP an acceptable fallback-level exit (90 days' written notice for any reason after the one-year Initial Term, and the Initial Term itself is not longer than 12 months), and the only termination-related payment is fees generated during the 90-day termination period, i.e. no more than three months' fees. It fails the fallback on one material term: the right is mutual and untethered, so Kubient may walk away for convenience mid-term during any renewal term. An auto-renewal/notice mechanic is not term-end-only unless the effective date is expressly tied to the end of the then-current term, so this is Vendor mid-term convenience termination rather than mere non-renewal. Our edit is the shortest conforming change: it preserves AP's 90-day right verbatim and confines Kubient's convenience termination to the end of the then-current Term, keeping its 90 days' notice. We have not pursued the preferred position (30 days' notice, pro-rata refund of prepaid fees), which is a poor fit for this revenue-share model with no prepaid fees.

Processing to provide, secure, support, or improve the Services for Customer is service delivery, not independent exploitation. **Finding submitted: deviation (LICENSE), fallback-level cure.**

- **Responsive locations inspected:** the sole grant clause, section 2 (p0002); the licence definitions (p0003–p0014); the termination-consequence revocation (p0021); the use restrictions/third-party access bar (p0025); and the assignment clause (p0072).
- **Why it fails fallback:** the grant runs only to "Customer" (defined at p0000 as The Associated Press alone — no affiliate inclusion, so no duplicate coverage risk), with no affiliate/contractor path, and it is expressly "non-transferable, non-assignable", which as the specific provision defeats reliance on the general successor-assignment right in p0072.
- **Cure (one operation):** affiliates identified in written notice are added as licensees and the licence is made transferable to an M&A successor, by deleting only the conflicting "non-transferable, non-assignable," words and keeping the remainder of the grant verbatim.
- **Noted, not flagged:** the licence remains "revocable" and section 4(c)(ii) revokes it on termination — short of preferred, but deleting "revocable" would require collateral conforming edits to section 4(a)'s mutual convenience termination (which benefits us) and to 4(c)(ii), so the fallback edit is the shortest complete position.

You are an independent verifier of one proposed customer-side contract redline in a fresh context.
Treat the preferred and fallback positions as separate atomic checklists. Evaluate the operative rendered language, not the drafter's confidence or margin comment. Copy every supplied element string exactly into the corresponding output item, assess both levels, and return met, not_met, or cannot_tell with concise textual evidence. A conditional element is met when its stated condition does not apply, but explain why.

Apply rule boundaries: voluntary use of one Vendor interface is not a sole-supplier promise when Customer remains free to use alternatives; a disclosure, right-to-match, or most-favoured offer mechanic is MFN rather than exclusivity unless alternatives remain prohibited after compliance; natural-term non-renewal is evaluated under RENEWAL, not as mid-term T4C; an unconditional Customer election to terminate is a convenience right. An auto-renewal clause permitting either party to terminate on notice does not make Vendor termination term-end-only unless the termination effective date is expressly tied to the end of the then-current term. A broad Vendor right to distribute, resell, independently exploit Customer Data, or use it for the wider "purposes contemplated by this Agreement" defeats the solely-to-provide-the-Services element even if ownership nominally remains with Customer. Processing to provide, secure, support, or improve the Services for Customer remains service delivery. A prohibition on another use unless Customer later gives express written consent is not itself a standing Vendor licence.

Fail intent if a Customer-only successor or licence-transfer element is implemented by granting Vendor a new assignment exception. A Customer Data insurance trigger must cover every category of data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for Customer, not merely selected named data types. Cosmetic deletion or paraphrase of words outside the target elements fails minimality.

For ASSIGN fallback, any retained no-consent non-successor exception—including a mutual affiliate exception—defeats "Other assignments require consent." Under LICENSE, resolve whether Customer already includes affiliates and fail minimality for duplicate coverage. A grant to an affiliate ordinarily permits use through its authorized personnel; a separate personnel/access edit is unnecessary unless retained language expressly contradicts the new grant. A broad notwithstanding override of the assignment clause is non-minimal when a direct "without Vendor approval" transfer permission will do.

The redline is position-complete when every element at either the preferred level or the fallback level is met. Do not mark a level complete if an element is omitted, merely promised in the comment, internally inconsistent, or depends on an undefined trigger. Deterministic regexes are evidence; inspect their result in substance as well as mechanically.

Minimal means the proposal changes only what is needed to reach one complete level, retains favourable existing language, avoids duplicating operative terms, and adds no requirement outside the chosen checklist. Treat model-language extras as extras: survival tails, at-own-expense language, additional damages categories, procedures, or boilerplate fail minimality unless a selected element requires them. For a missing clause, a concise insertion can be minimal even though all its words are new. Preserves intent means unrelated allocation, timing, remedies, references, and commercial mechanics survive without contradiction; fail intent if an edit leaves an undefined term, dangling cross-reference, or contradictory retained sentence.

Read nouns, modifiers, temporal anchors, amounts, bases, scope, and party direction literally. Do not infer "pro rata" merely from a refund that covers a post-termination period. Do not equate broader "all amounts paid or payable" with "fees paid or payable", "the 12 months preceding the event giving rise to a claim" with "the 12 months preceding the claim", or a deadline running from a request with one running from termination. A customary other-court carve-out solely for temporary injunctive relief preserves an otherwise exclusive merits forum; a broader alternate forum does not. A "no field-of-use restriction" result is not complete while an exclusive Vendor right prevents Customer use of its own product or brand. Fail minimality when a fallback proposal exceeds its numeric threshold without necessity. A no-liquidated-damages result must be unconditional and leave no retained formula, instalment, or contingent payment mechanic. Treat removal of any word outside the chosen elements—even a Customer-favourable restriction—as a minimality failure. Do not infer an omitted element from general commercial context.

For a liability cap, resolve the definition used by any Customer-payment carve-out. Language excluding only a narrowly defined subset of Fees does not cover Customer payment obligations as a whole. Treat explanatory examples added to an otherwise complete formula as non-minimal.

For T4C, treat "in whole or in part" as surplus unless the selected checklist and an actual Order Form or partial-termination structure require it.

For TRANSITION, the stated assistance period must apply after every covered expiry or termination; a request condition tied only to anticipated expiry does not suffice. Certified deletion must occur after data return. For WARRANTY fallback, do not treat reports, outputs, or services as software merely because they conform to a manual; require an express software-to-documentation warranty unless the contract defines the item as software.

Give actionable reasons. If an element is not met, name the exact defect the drafter must repair in operative language.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Rule and exact checklists:
ID: LICENSE
Title: Licence grant scope
Kind: parametric
Summary: The licence must cover our affiliates and contractors and must not be revocable at will.
Severity: high
Category: licence
Position — preferred:
Licence extends to Customer's affiliates and to contractors acting on Customer's behalf; paid-up licences are perpetual and irrevocable; subscription licences terminable only for uncured material breach; transferable to successors.

Position — fallback:
Affiliates covered on written notice; transferable to a successor in an M&A transaction.
Position — walk-away:
Licence revocable at Vendor's discretion; affiliates and contractors excluded with no path to add them.
Detection guidance:
Find the grant clause: "non-exclusive, non-transferable", "revocable", "solely for Customer's internal use", whether affiliates/contractors are named, term of the licence.

Redline guidance:
Insert "and its Affiliates and contractors acting on its behalf", delete "revocable", add successor transfer.

Preferred atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "The licence extends to Customer's affiliates.",
  "The licence extends to contractors acting on Customer's behalf.",
  "A paid-up licence is perpetual.",
  "A paid-up licence is irrevocable.",
  "A subscription licence is terminable only for uncured material breach.",
  "The licence is transferable to Customer's successors."
]

Fallback atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Customer's affiliates are covered on written notice.",
  "The licence is transferable to a successor in a merger or acquisition transaction."
]

Claimed finding status: deviation

Claimed target and element mapping:

The only licence grant (section 2, p0002) runs to "Customer" alone — a defined term limited to The Associated Press itself, with no affiliate or contractor coverage and no notice mechanic to add them — and it is expressly "non-transferable, non-assignable", so the licence cannot follow Customer into a merger or acquisition. The general assignment clause (p0072) permits assignment of the Agreement to a successor, but the specific licence prohibition overrides it for the licence itself, so the successor-transfer element is not already met. The clause therefore fails both fallback elements. We took the fallback target: affiliates covered on written notice and transferability to an M&A successor, in one surgical edit. We deliberately did not chase the preferred position (deleting "revocable" and limiting revocation to uncured material breach) because that would require collateral conforming rewrites of section 4(a)'s mutual post-Initial-Term termination right and section 4(c)(ii)'s revocation-on-termination mechanic; we note the licence remains revocable, which is short of preferred.

Each Party hereby irrevocably submits for all disputes to the exclusive jurisdiction and venue of the state and federal courts located in New York, New York.
input.rationale: Section 14(a) picks Delaware law (an accepted fallback law) but pairs it with New York courts, so it matches neither the preferred position (New York law plus New York County courts) nor the fallback (Delaware/California law with the corresponding courts). More materially, Section 8 imposes mandatory AAA arbitration for "[a]ny controversy or claim arising out of or relating to this Agreement", which directly contradicts the exclusive court jurisdiction in Section 14(a) and means the contract does not deliver a court forum at all; the fallback forum element therefore fails on a material term. The seat is domestic AAA rather than a foreign arbitration, so this is a deviation rather than walk-away. Our redline makes New York the governing law (matching both parties' home jurisdiction and the venue already agreed) and conforms Section 8 to exclusive merits resolution in the state and federal courts in New York County, retaining the customary temporary-injunctive-relief carve-out. The jury waiver and one-year limitation sentences in Section 8, and the fee-shifting reference in 14(d), are left untouched as outside this rule.

You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use document tools to inspect every responsive clause, definition, and cross-reference; do not stop at the first hit.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and never flag an obligation that benefits our party.

Keep rule boundaries precise. A sourcing requirement that applies only when Customer voluntarily uses Vendor's interface is not exclusivity when Customer is expressly free to use alternatives. A disclosure, right-to-match, or most-favoured offer mechanic belongs under MFN and is not also exclusivity unless it outright prohibits using alternatives after the mechanic is honoured. Natural-term non-renewal belongs under RENEWAL and is not Vendor mid-term termination for convenience under T4C; do not flag the same term twice. An unconditional Customer election to terminate is a convenience right even if the clause does not use the word "convenience". An auto-renewal clause that either party may terminate on notice does not establish that Vendor termination is term-end-only unless the effective date is expressly tied to the end of the then-current term. Under IP, inspect every Customer Data licence: distribution, resale, independent exploitation, or use for the broader "purposes contemplated by this Agreement" is not cured by adding a separate ownership sentence and must be narrowed expressly to processing solely to provide the Services. Processing to provide, secure, support, or improve the Services for Customer is service delivery, not independent exploitation. A prohibition on another use unless Customer later gives express written consent is not a standing Vendor licence; do not flag that hypothetical consent alone.

Do not weaken Customer while completing an element. A Customer licence-transfer right does not justify expanding a mutual assignment exception for Vendor; draft a Customer-only licence transfer. A conditional insurance element covering Customer Data must reach every category of data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for Customer; do not narrow it to a few named examples. When inserting qualifiers into an existing clause, keep every untouched word verbatim rather than cosmetically rewriting the whole sentence.

For ASSIGN fallback, "other assignments require consent" means every non-successor assignment: a retained no-consent affiliate exception conflicts with that level, even when mutual. A licence grant to an entity ordinarily reaches that entity's authorized personnel, so do not rewrite a separate personnel/access clause unless it expressly prohibits use needed by the new grant. Express a permitted licence transfer directly (for example, "without Vendor's approval"); do not add a broad notwithstanding override of the assignment clause.

The preferred and fallback positions are operative checklists, not drafting themes. First classify under the supplied playbook semantics. If the existing bargain meets every fallback element on its material terms, submit compliant and do not upgrade it merely to reach preferred wording. If it genuinely fails fallback, choose a preferred or fallback target and make the shortest operative change that meets every element at that target level.

For every deviation or missing proposal, map each target element exactly once in elementCoverage. Before drafting, search for each element independently. Use already_met only with a verbatim document quote, cite that quote's paragraph in paragraphIds, and do not restate an already-met element in a new operation. Use addressed_by_operation with one-based operationIndexes. You may leave an element unaddressed only by submitting needs_review with a concrete explanation. Never claim that a margin comment cures missing operative language.

Draft surgically: replace only the existing words or sentence that need to change, group related elements into one operation, and preserve unrelated text. When curing a prohibition, edit the prohibitory operator and duration or use one short affirmative permission; do not both negate the restriction and recite every permitted activity. Avoid a broad "notwithstanding" override when a precise conforming edit can resolve the conflict. After rendering, inspect every retained reference to a term or sentence you changed: an undefined term, dangling cross-reference, or contradictory retained mechanic is an intent failure. Prefer a fallback edit when deleting to preferred would require collateral rewrites. A replace may add at most 1.5 times as many words as it removes. For a genuinely absent clause, use insert_after and draft the shortest clause that carries only the still-missing target elements; do not rewrite a neighbouring clause.

The atomic checklist is the ceiling as well as the floor. Model language and precedents are source material, not permission to add non-element boilerplate. Omit survival tails, at-own-expense language, incidental or special damages, procedures, and other ancillary terms unless a selected element requires them. Meet numeric floors and ceilings at the selected threshold; do not volunteer a more onerous duration or amount just because it appears at the other level. Preserve exact nouns, temporal anchors, and bases: "fees paid or payable" may not become broader "all amounts paid or payable", and "preceding the claim" is not interchangeable with "preceding the event giving rise to the claim." Preserve every word in a mixed phrase that the target does not require changing: for example, curing "without reduction or termination rights" must not silently remove the reduction restriction. A customary other-court carve-out solely for temporary injunctive relief does not defeat an otherwise exclusive merits forum. A preferred "no non-compete or field-of-use restriction" is not met while Vendor retains an exclusive right that prevents Customer from using or licensing its own product or brand. Do not add terms that are absent from the selected checklist.

For a preferred no-liquidated-damages result, make the prohibition unconditional and conform every retained formula, instalment, or "if any" payment mechanic; otherwise use the exact fallback cap instead. Defining a payment as zero while retaining machinery that contemplates it is not a clean cure.

For T4C, do not add "in whole or in part" or a partial-termination right unless the selected element and this contract's Order Form structure require it.

For TRANSITION, the selected assistance duration must be available after every covered expiry or termination; a pre-expiry request condition does not establish a post-termination duration. State that certified deletion occurs after data return, not merely after assistance. For WARRANTY fallback, a report or output conforming to a user manual is not a software-to-documentation warranty unless that report is itself the defined software deliverable; add the shortest express software conformance warranty when needed.

For a preferred liability cap, verify the definition behind every payment-carve-out noun. A carve-out limited to a narrowly defined "Fees" category does not exclude all Customer payment obligations; surgically use "amounts due" or equally comprehensive operative language. Do not add explanatory examples such as "including subscription fees" to the cap formula when lowercase fees under the Agreement and all Order Forms is sufficient.

Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Finding quotes must be 600 characters or fewer. Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and accurately explain the operative change.

input.rationale: Section 14(a) picks Delaware law (an accepted fallback law) but pairs it with New York courts, so it matches neither the preferred position (New York law plus New York County courts) nor the fallback (Delaware/California law with the corresponding courts). More materially, Section 8 imposes mandatory AAA arbitration for "[a]ny controversy or claim arising out of or relating to this Agreement", which directly contradicts the exclusive court jurisdiction in Section 14(a) and means the contract does not deliver a court forum at all; the fallback forum element therefore fails on a material term. The seat is domestic AAA rather than a foreign arbitration, so this is a deviation rather than walk-away. Our redline makes New York the governing law (matching both parties' home jurisdiction and the venue already agreed) and conforms Section 8 to exclusive merits resolution in the state and federal courts in New York County, retaining the customary temporary-injunctive-relief carve-out. The jury waiver and one-year limitation sentences in Section 8, and the fee-shifting reference in 14(d), are left untouched as outside this rule.

Rule and exact checklists:
ID: ASSIGN
Title: Assignment and change of control
Kind: parametric
Summary: We may assign to affiliates and successors; the Vendor may not exit on our change of control.
Severity: high
Category: assignment
Position — preferred:
Customer may assign without consent to an affiliate or to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets; Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent (not to be unreasonably withheld) and never to a Customer competitor; no Vendor termination right on Customer's change of control.

Position — fallback:
Mutual right to assign to successors with written notice; consent for other assignments not unreasonably withheld.
Position — walk-away:

You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use document tools to inspect every responsive clause, definition, and cross-reference; do not stop at the first hit.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and never flag an obligation that benefits our party.

Keep rule boundaries precise. A sourcing requirement that applies only when Customer voluntarily uses Vendor's interface is not exclusivity when Customer is expressly free to use alternatives. A disclosure, right-to-match, or most-favoured offer mechanic belongs under MFN and is not also exclusivity unless it outright prohibits using alternatives after the mechanic is honoured. Natural-term non-renewal belongs under RENEWAL and is not Vendor mid-term termination for convenience under T4C; do not flag the same term twice. An unconditional Customer election to terminate is a convenience right even if the clause does not use the word "convenience". An auto-renewal clause that either party may terminate on notice does not establish that Vendor termination is term-end-only unless the effective date is expressly tied to the end of the then-current term. Under IP, inspect every Customer Data licence: distribution, resale, independent exploitation, or use for the broader "purposes contemplated by this Agreement" is not cured by adding a separate ownership sentence and must be narrowed expressly to processing solely to provide the Services. Processing to provide, secure, support, or improve the Services for Customer is service delivery, not independent exploitation. A prohibition on another use unless Customer later gives express written consent is not a standing Vendor licence; do not flag that hypothetical consent alone.

Do not weaken Customer while completing an element. A Customer licence-transfer right does not justify expanding a mutual assignment exception for Vendor; draft a Customer-only licence transfer. A conditional insurance element covering Customer Data must reach every category of data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for Customer; do not narrow it to a few named examples. When inserting qualifiers into an existing clause, keep every untouched word verbatim rather than cosmetically rewriting the whole sentence.

Resolve assignment and licence scope literally. For ASSIGN fallback, "other assignments require consent" means every non-successor assignment: a retained no-consent affiliate exception conflicts with that level, even when mutual. For LICENSE, first resolve whether the defined Customer already includes affiliates; do not add duplicate coverage. A licence grant to an entity ordinarily reaches that entity's authorized personnel, so do not rewrite a separate personnel/access clause unless it expressly prohibits use needed by the new grant. Express a permitted licence transfer directly (for example, "without Vendor's approval"); do not add a broad notwithstanding override of the assignment clause.

The preferred and fallback positions are operative checklists, not drafting themes. First classify under the supplied playbook semantics. If the existing bargain meets every fallback element on its material terms, submit compliant and do not upgrade it merely to reach preferred wording. If it genuinely fails fallback, choose a preferred or fallback target and make the shortest operative change that meets every element at that target level.

For every deviation or missing proposal, map each target element exactly once in elementCoverage. Before drafting, search for each element independently. Use already_met only with a verbatim document quote, cite that quote's paragraph in paragraphIds, and do not restate an already-met element in a new operation. Use addressed_by_operation with one-based operationIndexes. You may leave an element unaddressed only by submitting needs_review with a concrete explanation. Never claim that a margin comment cures missing operative language.

Draft surgically: replace only the existing words or sentence that need to change, group related elements into one operation, and preserve unrelated text. When curing a prohibition, edit the prohibitory operator and duration or use one short affirmative permission; do not both negate the restriction and recite every permitted activity. Avoid a broad "notwithstanding" override when a precise conforming edit can resolve the conflict. After rendering, inspect every retained reference to a term or sentence you changed: an undefined term, dangling cross-reference, or contradictory retained mechanic is an intent failure. Prefer a fallback edit when deleting to preferred would require collateral rewrites. A replace may add at most 1.5 times as many words as it removes. For a genuinely absent clause, use insert_after and draft the shortest clause that carries only the still-missing target elements; do not rewrite a neighbouring clause.

The atomic checklist is the ceiling as well as the floor. Model language and precedents are source material, not permission to add non-element boilerplate. Omit survival tails, at-own-expense language, incidental or special damages, procedures, and other ancillary terms unless a selected element requires them. Meet numeric floors and ceilings at the selected threshold; do not volunteer a more onerous duration or amount just because it appears at the other level. Preserve exact nouns, temporal anchors, and bases: "fees paid or payable" may not become broader "all amounts paid or payable", and "preceding the claim" is not interchangeable with "preceding the event giving rise to the claim." Preserve every word in a mixed phrase that the target does not require changing: for example, curing "without reduction or termination rights" must not silently remove the reduction restriction. A customary other-court carve-out solely for temporary injunctive relief does not defeat an otherwise exclusive merits forum. A preferred "no non-compete or field-of-use restriction" is not met while Vendor retains an exclusive right that prevents Customer from using or licensing its own product or brand. Do not add terms that are absent from the selected checklist.

For a preferred no-liquidated-damages result, make the prohibition unconditional and conform every retained formula, instalment, or "if any" payment mechanic; otherwise use the exact fallback cap instead. Defining a payment as zero while retaining machinery that contemplates it is not a clean cure.

For T4C, do not add "in whole or in part" or a partial-termination right unless the selected element and this contract's Order Form structure require it.

For TRANSITION, the selected assistance duration must be available after every covered expiry or termination; a pre-expiry request condition does not establish a post-termination duration. State that certified deletion occurs after data return, not merely after assistance. For WARRANTY fallback, a report or output conforming to a user manual is not a software-to-documentation warranty unless that report is itself the defined software deliverable; add the shortest express software conformance warranty when needed.

For a preferred liability cap, verify the definition behind every payment-carve-out noun. A carve-out limited to a narrowly defined "Fees" category does not exclude all Customer payment obligations; surgically use "amounts due" or equally comprehensive operative language. - compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.

elements.evidence: Rendered 4(a): "Customer may terminate this Agreement for any reason following the Initial Term upon ninety (90) days written notice to Kubient" — an unconditional Customer election, i.e. a convenience right.

elements.evidence: "Kubient may do so only effective at the end of the then-current Term" — the effective date is expressly tied to term end, so Vendor cannot exit mid-term (that residual right is natural-term non-renewal, assessed under RENEWAL).

elements.evidence: "Customer may terminate this Agreement for any reason following the Initial Term upon ninety (90) days written notice to Kubient" — 90 days sits at the top of the 60–90 day band; the Initial Term is one (1) year, so the carve-out is not a multi-year lock-in.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: The only payment mechanic retained is "Kubient shall be entitled to all fees generated during the termination period" — fees earned in the ordinary course during the 90-day notice period, not a separate early-termination fee or penalty; the capping condition therefore does not bite.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: "Kubient may do so only effective at the end of the then-current Term" expressly ties the effective date of Vendor's convenience termination to term end, which is what the rule requires of an otherwise mutual notice mechanic.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination.
elements.evidence: The edit converted the mutual sentence into a Customer-only predicate ("upon ninety (90) days written notice to Kubient") and then attaches Vendor by the shorthand "Kubient may do so only effective at the end of the then-current Term". reasons: Fallback is incomplete on one element: after the split, the 90-day notice obligation runs only in Customer's favour ("written notice to Kubient"), and Kubient's obligation is carried solely by the pronoun "do so", whose antecedent names Kubient as the notice recipient. Repair by stating Vendor's right in full: "...; Kubient may terminate this Agreement for any reason upon ninety (90) days' prior written notice to Customer, such termination to be effective only at the end of the then-current Term."

The end-of-term confinement itself is correctly drafted — the effective date is expressly anchored to the end of the then-current Term, so the residual Vendor right is non-renewal rather than mid-term convenience termination, satisfying that fallback element and (incidentally) the preferred no-mid-term-Vendor-exit element.

Preferred level is not pursued and remains unmet (90 days rather than 30, and no pro-rata refund of prepaid fees); the rationale's explanation that this is a revenue-share model with no prepaid fees is a reasonable justification for targeting the fallback.

elements.element: Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
elements.evidence: No refund language anywhere in the rendered text; to the contrary, "Kubient shall be entitled to all fees generated during the termination period regardless of which Party terminates".

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: "Kubient may do so only effective at the end of the then-current Term" — the effective date is expressly tied to term end, so Vendor cannot exit mid-term (that residual right is natural-term non-renewal, assessed under RENEWAL).

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: "Customer may terminate this Agreement for any reason following the Initial Term upon ninety (90) days written notice to Kubient" — 90 days sits at the top of the 60–90 day band; the Initial Term is one (1) year, so the carve-out is not a multi-year lock-in.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: The only payment mechanic retained is "Kubient shall be entitled to all fees generated during the termination period" — fees earned in the ordinary course during the 90-day notice period, not a separate early-termination fee or penalty; the capping condition therefore does not bite.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: "Kubient may do so only effective at the end of the then-current Term" expressly ties the effective date of Vendor's convenience termination to term end, which is what the rule requires of an otherwise mutual notice mechanic.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination.
elements.evidence: The edit converted the mutual sentence into a Customer-only predicate ("upon ninety (90) days written notice to Kubient") and then attaches Vendor by the shorthand "Kubient may do so only effective at the end of the then-current Term". Read literally, "do so" imports a notice given "to Kubient", i.e. Vendor noticing itself; no operative sentence obliges Kubient to give Customer 90 days' written notice, and the only express constraint on Kubient is the effective date, not a notice period.

Unmet fallback elements (copy these exact strings into the repaired coverage):
- Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination.
  Verdict: not_met. Evidence: The edit converted the mutual sentence into a Customer-only predicate ("upon ninety (90) days written notice to Kubient") and then attaches Vendor by the shorthand "Kubient may do so only effective at the end of the then-current Term". Read literally, "do so" imports a notice given "to Kubient", i.e. Vendor noticing itself; no operative sentence obliges Kubient to give Customer 90 days' written notice, and the only express constraint on Kubient is the effective date, not a notice period.

Verifier reasons:
- Fallback is incomplete on one element: after the split, the 90-day notice obligation runs only in Customer's favour ("written notice to Kubient"), and Kubient's obligation is carried solely by the pronoun "do so", whose antecedent names Kubient as the notice recipient. Repair by stating Vendor's right in full: "...; Kubient may terminate this Agreement for any reason upon ninety (90) days' prior written notice to Customer, such termination to be effective only at the end of the then-current Term."
- The end-of-term confinement itself is correctly drafted — the effective date is expressly anchored to the end of the then-current Term, so the residual Vendor right is non-renewal rather than mid-term convenience termination, satisfying that fallback element and (incidentally) the preferred no-mid-term-Vendor-exit element.
- Early-termination fee element is satisfied without change: "all fees generated during the termination period" is ordinary revenue earned while the Agreement continues through the notice period, not a penalty; consider clarifying that for a Kubient end-of-term termination the "termination period" means the 90-day notice period, so the retained fee sentence cannot be read to stretch beyond three months.
- Preferred level is not pursued and remains unmet (90 days rather than 30, and no pro-rata refund of prepaid fees); the rationale's explanation that this is a revenue-share model with no prepaid fees is a reasonable justification for targeting the fallback.
- Minimality holds: the edit touches only the mutual convenience sentence, retains the Initial Term lock, the breach/insolvency rights in 4(b) and the fee sentence verbatim, and adds no extras (no survival tail, refund mechanic, or procedure) beyond the selected checklist.
- Intent is preserved: renewal mechanics, breach termination, and the fee allocation survive without contradiction; the only defect is the unspecified Vendor notice recipient/period identified above, which is an element gap rather than a collateral change.

system.text:
You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use document tools to inspect every responsive clause, definition, and cross-reference; do not stop at the first hit.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and never flag an obligation that benefits our party.

Keep rule boundaries precise. A sourcing requirement that applies only when Customer voluntarily uses Vendor's interface is not exclusivity when Customer is expressly free to use alternatives. A disclosure, right-to-match, or most-favoured offer mechanic belongs under MFN and is not also exclusivity unless it outright prohibits using alternatives after the mechanic is honoured. Natural-term non-renewal belongs under RENEWAL and is not Vendor mid-term termination for convenience under T4C; do not flag the same term twice. An unconditional Customer election to terminate is a convenience right even if the clause does not use the word "convenience". An auto-renewal clause that either party may terminate on notice does not establish that Vendor termination is term-end-only unless the effective date is expressly tied to the end of the then-current term. Under IP, inspect every Customer Data licence: distribution, resale, independent exploitation, or use for the broader "purposes contemplated by this Agreement" is not cured by adding a separate ownership sentence and must be narrowed expressly to processing solely to provide the Services. Processing to provide, secure, support, or improve the Services for Customer is service delivery, not independent exploitation. A prohibition on another use unless Customer later gives express written consent is not a standing Vendor licence; do not flag that hypothetical consent alone.

Do not weaken Customer while completing an element. A Customer licence-transfer right does not justify expanding a mutual assignment exception for Vendor; draft a Customer-only licence transfer. A conditional insurance element covering Customer Data must reach every category of data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for Customer; do not narrow it to a few named examples. When inserting qualifiers into an existing clause, keep every untouched word verbatim rather than cosmetically rewriting the whole sentence.

Resolve assignment and licence scope literally. For ASSIGN fallback, "other assignments require consent" means every non-successor assignment: a retained no-consent affiliate exception conflicts with that level, even when mutual. For LICENSE, first resolve whether the defined Customer already includes affiliates; do not add duplicate coverage. A licence grant to an entity ordinarily reaches that entity's authorized personnel, so do not rewrite a separate personnel/access clause unless it expressly prohibits use needed by the new grant. Express a permitted licence transfer directly (for example, "without Vendor's approval"); do not add a broad notwithstanding override of the assignment clause.

The preferred and fallback positions are operative checklists, not drafting themes. First classify under the supplied playbook semantics. If the existing bargain meets every fallback element on its material terms, submit compliant and do not upgrade it merely to reach preferred wording. If it genuinely fails fallback, choose a preferred or fallback target and make the shortest operative change that meets every element at that target level.

For every deviation or missing proposal, map each target element exactly once in elementCoverage. Before drafting, search for each element independently. Use already_met only with a verbatim document quote, cite that quote's paragraph in paragraphIds, and do not restate an already-met element in a new operation. Use addressed_by_operation with one-based operationIndexes. You may leave an element unaddressed only by submitting needs_review with a concrete explanation. Never claim that a margin comment cures missing operative language.

Draft surgically: replace only the existing words or sentence that need to change, group related elements into one operation, and preserve unrelated text. When curing a prohibition, edit the prohibitory operator and duration or use one short affirmative permission; do not both negate the restriction and recite every permitted activity. Avoid a broad "notwithstanding" override when a precise conforming edit can resolve the conflict. After rendering, inspect every retained reference to a term or sentence you changed: an undefined term, dangling cross-reference, or contradictory retained mechanic is an intent failure. Prefer a fallback edit when deleting to preferred would require collateral rewrites. A replace may add at most 1.5 times as many words as it removes. For a genuinely absent clause, use insert_after and draft the shortest clause that carries only the still-missing target elements; do not rewrite a neighbouring clause.

The atomic checklist is the ceiling as well as the floor. Model language and precedents are source material, not permission to add non-element boilerplate. Omit survival tails, at-own-expense language, incidental or special damages, procedures, and other ancillary terms unless a selected element requires them. Meet numeric floors and ceilings at the selected threshold; do not volunteer a more onerous duration or amount just because it appears at the other level. Preserve exact nouns, temporal anchors, and bases: "fees paid or payable" may not become broader "all amounts paid or payable", and "preceding the claim" is not interchangeable with "preceding the event giving rise to the claim." Preserve every word in a mixed phrase that the target does not require changing: for example, curing "without reduction or termination rights" must not silently remove the reduction restriction. A customary other-court carve-out solely for temporary injunctive relief does not defeat an otherwise exclusive merits forum. A preferred "no non-compete or field-of-use restriction" is not met while Vendor retains an exclusive right that prevents Customer from using or licensing its own product or brand. Do not add terms that are absent from the selected checklist.

For a preferred no-liquidated-damages result, make the prohibition unconditional and conform every retained formula, instalment, or "if any" payment mechanic; otherwise use the exact fallback cap instead. Defining a payment as zero while retaining machinery that contemplates it is not a clean cure.

For T4C, do not add "in whole or in part" or a partial-termination right unless the selected element and this contract's Order Form structure require it.

For TRANSITION, the selected assistance duration must be available after every covered expiry or termination; a pre-expiry request condition does not establish a post-termination duration. State that certified deletion occurs after data return, not merely after assistance. For WARRANTY fallback, a report or output conforming to a user manual is not a software-to-documentation warranty unless that report is itself the defined software deliverable; add the shortest express software conformance warranty when needed.

For a preferred liability cap, verify the definition behind every payment-carve-out noun. A carve-out limited to a narrowly defined "Fees" category does not exclude all Customer payment obligations; surgically use "amounts due" or equally comprehensive operative language. Do not add explanatory examples such as "including subscription fees" to the cap formula when lowercase fees under the Agreement and all Order Forms is sufficient.

Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Finding quotes must be 600 characters or fewer. Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and accurately explain the operative change.

For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding. For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Parties: we represent The Associated Press; counterparty is Kubient Inc..

Rule and atomic checklists:
ID: T4C
Title: Termination for convenience
Kind: parametric
Summary: We can leave on notice without penalty; the Vendor cannot walk away mid-term.
Severity: high
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Customer may terminate for convenience on 30 days' written notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees; Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.

Position — fallback:
Customer termination on 60–90 days' notice; early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees; Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term on 90 days' notice.

Position — walk-away:
No Customer right to terminate for convenience in a multi-year term; Vendor termination for convenience on fewer than 90 days' notice.

Detection guidance:
Find termination provisions. Determine which party may terminate without cause, the notice period, and any early-termination fee. Absence of any Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months is a deviation (kind: missing behaviour); a Vendor convenience right on short notice is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Add or edit a Customer convenience right (30 days), delete/limit Vendor's convenience right, replace penalties with the fallback fee cap.

Model language:
Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination.


Preferred atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.",
  "Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.",
  "Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.",
  "Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term."
]

Fallback atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.",
  "Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.",
  "Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.",
  "Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination."
]

input.rationale: Paragraph 4(a) is the only termination-for-convenience mechanic in the Agreement. It gives AP an acceptable fallback-level exit (90 days' written notice for any reason after the one-year Initial Term, and the Initial Term itself is not longer than 12 months), and the only termination-related payment is fees generated during the 90-day termination period, i.e. no more than three months' fees. It fails the fallback on one material term: the right is mutual and untethered, so Kubient may walk away for convenience mid-term during any renewal term. An auto-renewal/notice mechanic is not term-end-only unless the effective date is expressly tied to the end of the then-current term, so this is Vendor mid-term convenience termination rather than mere non-renewal. Our edit is the shortest conforming change: it preserves AP's 90-day right verbatim and confines Kubient's convenience termination to the end of the then-current Term, keeping its 90 days' notice. We have not pursued the preferred position (30 days' notice, pro-rata refund of prepaid fees), which is a poor fit for this revenue-share model with no prepaid fees.

content.text:
**Finding submitted: deviation (T4C), fallback-level cure.**

- **Only responsive clause:** paragraph 4(a) (p0016). No other convenience-termination or early-termination-fee mechanic exists (4(b) is breach/insolvency; §5 is a revenue share with no prepaid fees; 4(c) is effects of termination).
- **What passes fallback:** AP has a 90-day for-any-reason exit after the Initial Term (which is exactly 12 months, so the lock-in is not itself a deviation), and the only termination-linked payment is fees generated during the 90-day termination period — within the three-months-of-fees cap.
- **What fails:** the right is mutual and not tied to term-end, so Kubient could exit for convenience mid-renewal-term. Per the playbook, an auto-renewal/notice right is not term-end-only unless the effective date is expressly anchored to the end of the then-current term — this is Vendor mid-term convenience termination, not non-renewal.
- **Cure:** one surgical replace splitting the mutual sentence — AP's 90-day right preserved verbatim, Kubient's termination effective only at the end of the then-current Term, with its 90 days' notice carried through by "do so." Minimality gate returned ok:true.

Evidence: The edit converted the mutual sentence into a Customer-only predicate ("upon ninety (90) days written notice to Kubient") and then attaches Vendor by the shorthand "Kubient may do so only effective at the end of the then-current Term". Read literally, "do so" imports a notice given "to Kubient", i.e. Vendor noticing itself; no operative sentence obliges Kubient to give Customer 90 days' written notice, and the only express constraint on Kubient is the effective date, not a notice period.

Verifier reasons:
- Fallback is incomplete on one element: after the split, the 90-day notice obligation runs only in Customer's favour ("written notice to Kubient"), and Kubient's obligation is carried solely by the pronoun "do so", whose antecedent names Kubient as the notice recipient. Repair by stating Vendor's right in full: "...; Kubient may terminate this Agreement for any reason upon ninety (90) days' prior written notice to Customer, such termination to be effective only at the end of the then-current Term."
- The end-of-term confinement itself is correctly drafted — the effective date is expressly anchored to the end of the then-current Term, so the residual Vendor right is non-renewal rather than mid-term convenience termination, satisfying that fallback element and (incidentally) the preferred no-mid-term-Vendor-exit element.
- Early-termination fee element is satisfied without change: "all fees generated during the termination period" is ordinary revenue earned while the Agreement continues through the notice period, not a penalty; consider clarifying that for a Kubient end-of-term termination the "termination period" means the 90-day notice period, so the retained fee sentence cannot be read to stretch beyond three months.
- Preferred level is not pursued and remains unmet (90 days rather than 30, and no pro-rata refund of prepaid fees); the rationale's explanation that this is a revenue-share model with no prepaid fees is a reasonable justification for targeting the fallback.
- Minimality holds: the edit touches only the mutual convenience sentence, retains the Initial Term lock, the breach/insolvency rights in 4(b) and the fee sentence verbatim, and adds no extras (no survival tail, refund mechanic, or procedure) beyond the selected checklist.
- Intent is preserved: renewal mechanics, breach termination, and the fee allocation survive without contradiction; the only defect is the unspecified Vendor notice recipient/period identified above, which is an element gap rather than a collateral change.
