[
  "Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.",
  "Vendor provides transition assistance for up to six months.",
  "Transition assistance is charged at then-current rates.",
  "Vendor returns Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.",
  "Customer Data is returned in a standard machine-readable format.",
  "Vendor certifies deletion of Customer Data after its return."
]

Fallback atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.",
  "Vendor provides at least 90 days of transition assistance.",

]

Finding rationale:
The only effect-of-termination provision (Section 4(c), p0019–p0022) requires Kubient to cease the Services, revokes the licence, and obliges each Party to "return or destroy" the other's Confidential Information. There is no transition assistance obligation and no obligation to export or return Customer's data (Requests, revenue/auction data or other data processed for AP) in any timeframe, and nothing elsewhere in the Agreement supplies it. The rule therefore fails at the fallback, so we insert a short clause at the fallback level: at least 90 days of transition assistance on expiry or termination and export of AP data within 30 days of expiry or termination. We have not volunteered the preferred six-month/machine-readable/certified-deletion package.

Original cited paragraphs:

p0020: (i) Kubient will cease providing the Services;
p0021: (ii) the license granted under section 3 shall be revoked, (iii) Customer will promptly cease use of the Services and the Auction Platform;

input.quote: Neither Party may terminate this Agreement during the Initial Term except as set forth in paragraph 4(b) or any Exhibit. Either Party may terminate this Agreement for any reason following the Initial Term upon ninety (90) days written notice to the other Party. Except for termination for material breach as detailed in paragraph 4(b), Kubient shall be entitled to all fees generated during the termination period regardless of which Party terminates the Agreement,
input.rationale: Paragraph 4(a) is the only convenience-termination mechanic in the Agreement and it fails the fallback in two material respects: AP has no no-cause exit during the Initial Term (the lock-in is mutual and the 90-day right operates only "following the Initial Term"), and Kubient's post-Initial Term right is untethered to term-end, so Kubient can walk away mid-renewal-term (an auto-renewal/notice right is not term-end-only unless the effective date is expressly anchored to the end of the then-current term). Our single edit confines the Initial Term lock-in to Kubient and splits the mutual sentence so that AP has an express right to terminate for convenience on 90 days' written notice to Kubient with no timing restriction, while Kubient's no-cause right expressly requires 90 days' written notice to AP and takes effect only at the end of the then-current Term. The retained fee sentence entitles Kubient only to fees generated during the termination period, i.e. revenue earned through the 90-day notice window, so no early-termination fee exceeding three months' fees exists. We do not pursue the preferred level (30 days' notice and pro-rata refund of prepaid fees), which is a poor fit for this revenue-share structure with no prepaid fees; the redline lands at the fallback.

system.text:
You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use document tools to inspect every responsive clause, definition, and cross-reference; do not stop at the first hit.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and never flag an obligation that benefits our party.

Keep rule boundaries precise. A sourcing requirement that applies only when Customer voluntarily uses Vendor's interface is not exclusivity when Customer is expressly free to use alternatives. A disclosure, right-to-match, or most-favoured offer mechanic belongs under MFN and is not also exclusivity unless it outright prohibits using alternatives after the mechanic is honoured. Natural-term non-renewal belongs under RENEWAL and is not Vendor mid-term termination for convenience under T4C; do not flag the same term twice. An unconditional Customer election to terminate is a convenience right even if the clause does not use the word "convenience". An auto-renewal clause that either party may terminate on notice does not establish that Vendor termination is term-end-only unless the effective date is expressly tied to the end of the then-current term. Under IP, inspect every Customer Data licence: distribution, resale, independent exploitation, or use for the broader "purposes contemplated by this Agreement" is not cured by adding a separate ownership sentence and must be narrowed expressly to processing solely to provide the Services. Processing to provide, secure, support, or improve the Services for Customer is service delivery, not independent exploitation. A prohibition on another use unless Customer later gives express written consent is not a standing Vendor licence; do not flag that hypothetical consent alone.

Do not weaken Customer while completing an element. A Customer licence-transfer right does not justify expanding a mutual assignment exception for Vendor; draft a Customer-only licence transfer. A conditional insurance element covering Customer Data must reach every category of data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for Customer; do not narrow it to a few named examples. When inserting qualifiers into an existing clause, keep every untouched word verbatim rather than cosmetically rewriting the whole sentence.

Resolve assignment and licence scope literally. For ASSIGN fallback, "other assignments require consent" means every non-successor assignment: a retained no-consent affiliate exception conflicts with that level, even when mutual. For LICENSE, first resolve whether the defined Customer already includes affiliates; do not add duplicate coverage. A licence grant to an entity ordinarily reaches that entity's authorized personnel, so do not rewrite a separate personnel/access clause unless it expressly prohibits use needed by the new grant. Express a permitted licence transfer directly (for example, "without Vendor's approval"); do not add a broad notwithstanding override of the assignment clause.

The preferred and fallback positions are operative checklists, not drafting themes. First classify under the supplied playbook semantics. If the existing bargain meets every fallback element on its material terms, submit compliant and do not upgrade it merely to reach preferred wording. If it genuinely fails fallback, choose a preferred or fallback target and make the shortest operative change that meets every element at that target level.

For every deviation or missing proposal, map each target element exactly once in elementCoverage. Before drafting, search for each element independently. Use already_met only with a verbatim document quote, cite that quote's paragraph in paragraphIds, and do not restate an already-met element in a new operation. Use addressed_by_operation with one-based operationIndexes. You may leave an element unaddressed only by submitting needs_review with a concrete explanation. Never claim that a margin comment cures missing operative language.

Draft surgically: replace only the existing words or sentence that need to change, group related elements into one operation, and preserve unrelated text. When curing a prohibition, edit the prohibitory operator and duration or use one short affirmative permission; do not both negate the restriction and recite every permitted activity. Avoid a broad "notwithstanding" override when a precise conforming edit can resolve the conflict. After rendering, inspect every retained reference to a term or sentence you changed: an undefined term, dangling cross-reference, or contradictory retained mechanic is an intent failure. Prefer a fallback edit when deleting to preferred would require collateral rewrites. A replace may add at most 1.5 times as many words as it removes. For a genuinely absent clause, use insert_after and draft the shortest clause that carries only the still-missing target elements; do not rewrite a neighbouring clause.

The atomic checklist is the ceiling as well as the floor. Model language and precedents are source material, not permission to add non-element boilerplate. Omit survival tails, at-own-expense language, incidental or special damages, procedures, and other ancillary terms unless a selected element requires them. Meet numeric floors and ceilings at the selected threshold; do not volunteer a more onerous duration or amount just because it appears at the other level. Preserve exact nouns, temporal anchors, and bases: "fees paid or payable" may not become broader "all amounts paid or payable", and "preceding the claim" is not interchangeable with "preceding the event giving rise to the claim." Preserve every word in a mixed phrase that the target does not require changing: for example, curing "without reduction or termination rights" must not silently remove the reduction restriction. A customary other-court carve-out solely for temporary injunctive relief does not defeat an otherwise exclusive merits forum. A preferred "no non-compete or field-of-use restriction" is not met while Vendor retains an exclusive right that prevents Customer from using or licensing its own product or brand. Do not add terms that are absent from the selected checklist.

For a preferred no-liquidated-damages result, make the prohibition unconditional and conform every retained formula, instalment, or "if any" payment mechanic; otherwise use the exact fallback cap instead. Defining a payment as zero while retaining machinery that contemplates it is not a clean cure.

For T4C, do not add "in whole or in part" or a partial-termination right unless the selected element and this contract's Order Form structure require it.

For TRANSITION, the selected assistance duration must be available after every covered expiry or termination; a pre-expiry request condition does not establish a post-termination duration. State that certified deletion occurs after data return, not merely after assistance. For WARRANTY fallback, a report or output conforming to a user manual is not a software-to-documentation warranty unless that report is itself the defined software deliverable; add the shortest express software conformance warranty when needed.

For a preferred liability cap, verify the definition behind every payment-carve-out noun. A carve-out limited to a narrowly defined "Fees" category does not exclude all Customer payment obligations; surgically use "amounts due" or equally comprehensive operative language. Do not add explanatory examples such as "including subscription fees" to the cap formula when lowercase fees under the Agreement and all Order Forms is sufficient.

Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Finding quotes must be 600 characters or fewer. Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and accurately explain the operative change.

For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding. For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

Parties: we represent The Associated Press; counterparty is Kubient Inc..

Rule and atomic checklists:
ID: T4C
Title: Termination for convenience
Kind: parametric
Summary: We can leave on notice without penalty; the Vendor cannot walk away mid-term.
Severity: high
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Customer may terminate for convenience on 30 days' written notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees; Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.

Position — fallback:
Customer termination on 60–90 days' notice; early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees; Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term on 90 days' notice.

Position — walk-away:
No Customer right to terminate for convenience in a multi-year term; Vendor termination for convenience on fewer than 90 days' notice.

Detection guidance:
Find termination provisions. Determine which party may terminate without cause, the notice period, and any early-termination fee. Absence of any Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months is a deviation (kind: missing behaviour); a Vendor convenience right on short notice is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Add or edit a Customer convenience right (30 days), delete/limit Vendor's convenience right, replace penalties with the fallback fee cap.

Model language:
Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination.

  "Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.",

  "Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term."
]

**Final finding submitted: deviation (T4C), fallback target.**

How I cleared the deterministic "Customer convenience termination present" failure without reintroducing the earlier element-4 gap:

- **AP's right is now named and express:** "Customer may terminate this Agreement for convenience upon ninety (90) days written notice to Kubient" — a Customer-specific, unqualified convenience right (no "following the Initial Term" timing bar, and the lock-in sentence now binds only Kubient).
- **Kubient's notice is stated in full, not by pronoun:** "Kubient may terminate this Agreement for any reason upon ninety (90) days written notice to Customer, effective only at the end of the then-current Term." This fixes the earlier "do so" defect (which read as Kubient noticing itself) while keeping the term-end anchor that removes Kubient's mid-term exit.
- **Coverage:** elements 1, 3 and 4 all sit in operative language in operation 1; the three-months fee cap stays `already_met` on the untouched fee-entitlement sentence.
- **Minimality/intent:** gate ok:true; the auto-renewal mechanic, the Exhibit carve-out, the fee sentence and 4(b) breach/insolvency rights are retained verbatim, "paragraph 4(b)" still resolves, and no extras (refunds, survival tails, "in whole or in part", procedures) were added. The two optional hardening items the verifier raised — defining "termination period" and trimming "or any Exhibit" — are outside the selected checklist, so I left them for the negotiation note rather than the redline.

system.text:
You are an independent verifier of one proposed customer-side contract redline in a fresh context.
Treat the preferred and fallback positions as separate atomic checklists. Evaluate the operative rendered language, not the drafter's confidence or margin comment. Copy every supplied element string exactly into the corresponding output item, assess both levels, and return met, not_met, or cannot_tell with concise textual evidence. A conditional element is met when its stated condition does not apply, but explain why.

Apply rule boundaries: voluntary use of one Vendor interface is not a sole-supplier promise when Customer remains free to use alternatives; a disclosure, right-to-match, or most-favoured offer mechanic is MFN rather than exclusivity unless alternatives remain prohibited after compliance; natural-term non-renewal is evaluated under RENEWAL, not as mid-term T4C; an unconditional Customer election to terminate is a convenience right. An auto-renewal clause permitting either party to terminate on notice does not make Vendor termination term-end-only unless the termination effective date is expressly tied to the end of the then-current term. A broad Vendor right to distribute, resell, independently exploit Customer Data, or use it for the wider "purposes contemplated by this Agreement" defeats the solely-to-provide-the-Services element even if ownership nominally remains with Customer. Processing to provide, secure, support, or improve the Services for Customer remains service delivery. A prohibition on another use unless Customer later gives express written consent is not itself a standing Vendor licence.

Fail intent if a Customer-only successor or licence-transfer element is implemented by granting Vendor a new assignment exception. A Customer Data insurance trigger must cover every category of data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for Customer, not merely selected named data types. Cosmetic deletion or paraphrase of words outside the target elements fails minimality.

For ASSIGN fallback, any retained no-consent non-successor exception—including a mutual affiliate exception—defeats "Other assignments require consent." Under LICENSE, resolve whether Customer already includes affiliates and fail minimality for duplicate coverage. A grant to an affiliate ordinarily permits use through its authorized personnel; a separate personnel/access edit is unnecessary unless retained language expressly contradicts the new grant. A broad notwithstanding override of the assignment clause is non-minimal when a direct "without Vendor approval" transfer permission will do.

The redline is position-complete when every element at either the preferred level or the fallback level is met. Do not mark a level complete if an element is omitted, merely promised in the comment, internally inconsistent, or depends on an undefined trigger. Deterministic regexes are evidence; inspect their result in substance as well as mechanically.

Minimal means the proposal changes only what is needed to reach one complete level, retains favourable existing language, avoids duplicating operative terms, and adds no requirement outside the chosen checklist. Treat model-language extras as extras: survival tails, at-own-expense language, additional damages categories, procedures, or boilerplate fail minimality unless a selected element requires them. For a missing clause, a concise insertion can be minimal even though all its words are new. Preserves intent means unrelated allocation, timing, remedies, references, and commercial mechanics survive without contradiction; fail intent if an edit leaves an undefined term, dangling cross-reference, or contradictory retained sentence.

Read nouns, modifiers, temporal anchors, amounts, bases, scope, and party direction literally. Do not infer "pro rata" merely from a refund that covers a post-termination period. Do not equate broader "all amounts paid or payable" with "fees paid or payable", "the 12 months preceding the event giving rise to a claim" with "the 12 months preceding the claim", or a deadline running from a request with one running from termination. A customary other-court carve-out solely for temporary injunctive relief preserves an otherwise exclusive merits forum; a broader alternate forum does not. A "no field-of-use restriction" result is not complete while an exclusive Vendor right prevents Customer use of its own product or brand. Fail minimality when a fallback proposal exceeds its numeric threshold without necessity. A no-liquidated-damages result must be unconditional and leave no retained formula, instalment, or contingent payment mechanic. Treat removal of any word outside the chosen elements—even a Customer-favourable restriction—as a minimality failure. Do not infer an omitted element from general commercial context.

For a liability cap, resolve the definition used by any Customer-payment carve-out. Language excluding only a narrowly defined subset of Fees does not cover Customer payment obligations as a whole. Treat explanatory examples added to an otherwise complete formula as non-minimal.

For T4C, treat "in whole or in part" as surplus unless the selected checklist and an actual Order Form or partial-termination structure require it.

For TRANSITION, the stated assistance period must apply after every covered expiry or termination; a request condition tied only to anticipated expiry does not suffice. Certified deletion must occur after data return. For WARRANTY fallback, do not treat reports, outputs, or services as software merely because they conform to a manual; require an express software-to-documentation warranty unless the contract defines the item as software.

Give actionable reasons. If an element is not met, name the exact defect the drafter must repair in operative language.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Position — preferred:

Customer termination on 60–90 days' notice; early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees; Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term on 90 days' notice.

No Customer right to terminate for convenience in a multi-year term; Vendor termination for convenience on fewer than 90 days' notice.

elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
elements.evidence: Rendered 4(a): "Customer may terminate this Agreement for convenience upon ninety (90) days written notice to Kubient" — an unconditional Customer election, and the element is satisfied by the Agreement-level right (no Order Form structure exists here).

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: The inserted Customer right requires "ninety (90) days written notice", three times the preferred 30-day maximum. To reach preferred the drafter would have to render the Customer notice period as thirty (30) days.

elements.element: Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
elements.evidence: No refund language appears anywhere in the rendered paragraph; the only money sentence runs the other way ("Kubient shall be entitled to all fees generated during the termination period"). A pro-rata refund of prepaid fees obligation would have to be added.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: Retained "Kubient may not terminate this Agreement during the Initial Term except as set forth in paragraph 4(b) or any Exhibit", plus the new limitation that Kubient's no-cause right is "effective only at the end of the then-current Term" — so no Kubient convenience termination takes effect during any committed term.

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: "Customer may terminate this Agreement for convenience upon ninety (90) days written notice to Kubient" — 90 days sits at the top of the 60–90 day band, and the timing bar was removed for Customer by limiting the Initial Term lock-in to Kubient, so the right is unconditional as to timing.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: Condition does not bite: the retained sentence ("Kubient shall be entitled to all fees generated during the termination period") entitles Kubient only to revenue actually generated through the 90-day notice window, not a penalty payable on early exit; read even at its widest it cannot exceed roughly three months of fees. No separate early-termination fee, formula or instalment survives.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: "Kubient may terminate this Agreement for any reason upon ninety (90) days written notice to Customer, effective only at the end of the then-current Term" — the effective date is expressly anchored to term end, satisfying the term-end-only requirement rather than a bare auto-renewal notice right.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination.
elements.evidence: Kubient's no-cause right requires "ninety (90) days written notice to Customer".

reasons: Fallback level is complete on the face of the operative text: Customer gets an unconditional 90-day convenience exit, Kubient's no-cause right is expressly effective only at the end of the then-current Term on 90 days' notice, and no early-termination penalty survives beyond fees actually generated during the notice window.

Preferred fails on two elements only — the Customer notice period is 90 rather than 30 days and there is no pro-rata prepaid-fee refund — which is consistent with the drafter's stated decision to land at the fallback in a revenue-share deal with no prepaid fees.

'deviation' is the correct finding status: the original clause locked Customer in for the Initial Term and gave Kubient a no-cause right "following the Initial Term" untethered to term end, so it failed the fallback on a material term.

Minimality holds. The two edits (confining the Initial Term bar to Kubient, and splitting the mutual sentence into a Customer convenience right and a term-end-anchored Kubient right) are each required by a selected fallback element. Favourable retained language survives untouched — the breach cure right, the insolvency right, the fee-entitlement sentence and the auto-renewal mechanic — and no survival tail, expense language, procedure or extra remedy was added.

Removal of the Customer half of the mutual Initial Term lock-in is inside the checklist, not an out-of-scope deletion: element 1 requires an unconditional Customer convenience right on 60–90 days' notice, which the retained "Neither Party may terminate ... during the Initial Term" would have blocked.

Intent is preserved: the Term/renewal structure, paragraph 4(b) cross-reference, Exhibit carve-out and fee allocation all survive without contradiction, and the edit creates no dangling reference or undefined new term (the pre-existing and unaltered phrase "the termination period" is inherited, not introduced).

If the client wants the preferred position, the two repairs are: change the Customer notice period to thirty (30) days, and add an express obligation that Kubient refund prepaid fees pro rata for the period after the effective date of termination.

You are in-house counsel producing a concise Markdown issues memo from verified findings.
Include: Executive summary; a Markdown table of findings with severity, rule, status and section; Walk-away items; Next steps.
Never invent a section reference or legal conclusion. Use only supplied findings.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

[{"id":"f-indemn-7c3c5e0c","ruleId":"INDEMN","ruleTitle":"Indemnification by Vendor","severity":"critical","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"Preamble","rationale":"Section 10(a) gives us an express Kubient duty to defend, indemnify and hold harmless AP and its officers, directors, managers, members, agents and employees against all third-party Claims arising out of the Services, the Auction Platform, Kubient's breach of any representation or warranty, and the acts or omissions of Kubient or its subcontractors. The clause therefore sits at or above the fallback and substantially meets the preferred position, and it is materially better than fallback in two respects that favour us: there are no Customer-modification/combination/specification exclusions, and Kubient's indemnity is not subject to any super-cap (§7(a) also carves indemnification out of the damages exclusion). There is therefore no perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify or sublicense deliverables, and no limitation on Kubient's use of AP Content, Requests or other AP data. That fails the fallback position on material terms, so we insert a single short paragraph at fallback level: Kubient keeps its generic tools, know-how and the Auction Platform; we take a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables (other than the Auction Platform, so paragraph 4(c) is not contradicted); and any Kubient licence in our data is limited to processing it solely to provide the Services.","proposal":"Insert an IP/data paragraph giving AP a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense Kubient deliverables, and limiting any Kubient licence in AP data to processing to provide the Services.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-lol-cap-df7f8e5e","ruleId":"LOL-CAP","ruleTitle":"Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs","severity":"critical","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"Preamble","rationale":"Section 7 (Limitation of Liability) contains only a mutual exclusion of consequential/indirect damages (with indemnification and confidentiality carved out of that exclusion). {"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Master Services Agreement (Kubient / The Associated Press)

**To:** Deal team
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side)
**Re:** Playbook review of Exhibit 10.14 Master Services Agreement, dated 5 February
**Status:** 18 rules assessed — 8 compliant, 7 deviations, 3 missing

---

## 1. Executive summary

The Agreement is structurally favourable to us on the commercial-freedom points: it imposes no exclusivity, no non-compete, no minimum commitment, no MFN, no non-solicit, no liquidated damages or penalties, and no Vendor audit right against us. Kubient's indemnity in Section 10(a), read with the Section 9(b) warranties and the Section 11 procedure, sits at or above our preferred position and is materially better than fallback in that it carries no super-cap and no modification/combination exclusions. We do not redline any of these.

The gaps are concentrated in risk allocation and exit. Three rules have no usable clause at all: there is no IP or data-ownership article (our only licence is a revocable, non-transferable licence to the Auction Platform that is revoked on termination); there is no insurance provision, for a vendor that collects, manages and stores visitor data under Section 9(b)(iii); and there is no transition assistance or data-export obligation, Section 4(c) requiring only that Services cease and Confidential Information be returned or destroyed. Seven further clauses fail the fallback on material terms: Section 7 excludes consequential damages but imposes **no aggregate cap at all**; the assignment carve-out in paragraph (h) runs to Kubient as well as to us, with no bar on assignment to our competitor; the Section 2 licence does not reach our affiliates and cannot follow us into an M&A transaction; paragraph 4(a) gives us no convenience exit during the Initial Term while letting Kubient exit mid-renewal-term and offering us no non-renewal notice right inside the 60-day fallback ceiling; Section 14(a) picks Delaware law with New York courts while Section 8 mandates AAA arbitration, so the contract delivers no coherent forum; and the warranty package has no documentation-conformance period and no repair, replacement or refund remedy.

Our proposed redlines are surgical and, where the preferred position is a poor fit for a revenue-share deal with no prepaid fees, land deliberately at fallback.

---

## 2. Findings

| # | Severity | Rule | Status | Section (as recorded) | Position / ask |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Compliant | Preamble | At or above preferred; uncapped and no combination exclusions. No redline (a fallback super-cap would weaken us). |
| 2 | Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | **Missing** | Preamble | Insert fallback-level paragraph: perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables (excluding the Auction Platform); Kubient's licence in our data limited to processing to provide the Services. |
| 3 | Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | **Deviation** | Preamble | Add mutual cap at the greater of 12 months' fees and USD 1,000,000, with uncapped Excluded Claims; our payment obligations outside the cap. Existing mutual consequential-damages exclusion retained. |
| 4 | High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | **Deviation** | Preamble | Make the affiliate/asset-purchaser/successor carve-out Customer-only; bar Kubient assignment to a Customer competitor. Balance of paragraph (h) unchanged. |
| 5 | High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Compliant | Preamble | Section 1 affirmatively disclaims exclusivity. No redline. |
| 6 | High | LD — Liquidated damages / penalties | Compliant | Preamble | No LDs, penalties, early-termination or minimum fee payable by us. No redline. |
| 7 | High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | **Deviation** | Preamble | Extend the Auction Platform licence to affiliates identified by written notice and make it transferable to an M&A successor. Revocability left as-is (short of preferred, by design). |
| 8 | High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Compliant | Preamble | No non-compete or field-of-use restriction on us. No redline. |
| 9 | High | T4C — Termination for convenience | **Deviation** | Preamble | Confine the Initial Term lock-in to Kubient; give us an express 90-day convenience right with no timing restriction; anchor Kubient's no-cause right to the end of the then-current Term. |
| 10 | Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | Preamble | No Vendor audit right exists; better than preferred. No redline. |
| 11 | Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | **Deviation** | Preamble | New York law; exclusive merits resolution in New York County state and federal courts in place of mandatory AAA arbitration, retaining the temporary-injunctive-relief carve-out. |
| 12 | Medium | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | **Missing** | Preamble | Insert new clause 14(j) at preferred limits: CGL 1M/2M, E&O 2M, cyber and privacy 5M where our data is handled, statutory workers' compensation, certificates on request. |
| 13 | Medium | MFN — MFN burdening Customer | Compliant | Preamble | No MFN, best-terms or right-to-match running to Kubient. No redline. |
| 14 | Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum commitments / volume restrictions | Compliant | Preamble | Pure revenue share; no minimum spend, take-or-pay or volume cap on us. No redline. |
| 15 | Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Compliant | Preamble | No restrictive covenant of any kind. No redline. |
| 16 | Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | **Deviation** | Preamble | Add a 60-day Customer non-renewal notice right; 1-year renewal terms are acceptable and no price-uplift mechanic exists. |
| 17 | Medium | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | **Missing** | Preamble | Insert fallback clause: at least 90 days' transition assistance on expiry or termination and export of our data within 30 days. |
| 18 | Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | **Deviation** | Preamble | Add 90-day software/deliverable documentation-conformance warranty, 30-day services warranty, and repair/replace or refund remedy. Section 13 disclaimer already preserves the express warranties. |

---

## 3. Walk-away items

1. **Vendor insurance (Finding 12 — missing).** The Agreement has no insurance provision anywhere in the body and no exhibits are attached, yet Kubient collects, maintains, manages and stores visitor data under paragraph 9(b)(iii) and serves creatives onto our Properties. Absence of insurance for a vendor processing our data is walk-away territory for us; we require the new clause 14(j), with fallback limits available in negotiation.
2. **Non-renewal notice window (Finding 16 — deviation, at the boundary).** Our only exit is termination for any reason following the Initial Term on 90 days' notice, an effective 90-day window that exceeds the 60-day fallback ceiling and sits at the walk-away boundary. We need the 60-day non-renewal right.
3. **Watch item — no liability cap (Finding 3).** Direct liability is currently unlimited on both sides. Not classified as walk-away, but we should not sign without the mutual cap and the Excluded Claims carve-outs; on a revenue-share deal a bare 12-months'-fees cap would be illusory, which is why we target the USD 1,000,000 floor.

---

## 4. Next steps

1. **Issue the redline** covering the seven deviations and three missing clauses, in the order of leverage: liability cap and insurance first, then IP/data ownership and transition assistance, then licence scope, assignment, termination/renewal, governing law and forum, and the warranty remedy.
2. **Resolve the forum conflict expressly.** Section 8's AAA arbitration mandate and Section 14(a)'s exclusive court jurisdiction contradict one another; our edit must conform both so the contract delivers a single forum. The Section 8 jury waiver, one-year limitation and the 14(d) fee-shifting reference are out of scope and stay untouched.
3. **Hold the line on the indemnity.** If Kubient reopens Section 10, do not trade our uncapped, exclusion-free indemnity for the playbook fallback structure. Optional upgrade asks only: name affiliates as indemnified parties and add a procure/modify/replace/refund ladder.
4. **Diligence the exhibits.** Commercial terms sit in the Exhibits and none is attached. Each executed Exhibit must be re-screened against MINCOMMIT (no minimum or shortfall), AUDIT (no usage or revenue-verification right; if one is sought, insert the preferred parameters — annual, 30 days' notice, independent auditor under confidentiality, off-site where possible, Vendor cost unless underpayment exceeds 5%, no direct system access) and EXCLUSIVITY (Section 5's default that Kubient contracts with all Advertisers is overridable in an Exhibit).
5. **QC before circulation.** The termination-for-convenience proposal (Finding 9) was flagged as repaired in verification; re-read that draft language against paragraph 4(a), including the retained-fee sentence, before the redline goes out.
6. **Note for the internal file.** Sub-preferred points we are consciously not redlining: the licence remains revocable; affiliates are not named indemnified parties and there is no indemnity remedy ladder; AP's reciprocal 10(b) indemnity is broader than preferred; and the preferred 12-month software warranty and six-month/machine-readable/certified-deletion transition package remain upgrade asks only."}
